artists.biography:
Steven John Wilson (born 3 November 1967) is an English musician, best known as the founder, lead guitarist, singer and songwriter of progressive rock band Porcupine Tree. He is involved in many other bands and musical projects both as musician and producer (including No-Man and Blackfield) and also maintains a solo career.
Wilson is a self-taught producer, audio engineer, guitar and keyboard player, playing other instruments as and where required (including bass guitar, concert harp, hammered dulcimer and flute).
He used to split his living time between Tel Aviv and London, England, but he no longer holds a permanent residence in Tel Aviv.

perplexity.description:
The Future Bites is the sixth studio album by British musician Steven Wilson, originally scheduled for release in 2020 but ultimately issued in January 2021 due to disruptions caused by the COVID-19 pandemic. Released through Caroline International, the album marks Wilson’s second and final project with the label. Musically, The Future Bites blends rock and pop with prominent electronic elements, expanding on the sonic experimentation of his previous work. The album incorporates dance and neo-disco influences while retaining a rock edge, particularly evident in the lead single "Personal Shopper." Wilson co-produced the record with David Kosten, crafting a sound that is both modern and reflective of his evolving style.

Thematically, The Future Bites explores identity and technology, offering a nuanced commentary on contemporary society rather than a purely dystopian vision. It stands as a distinct entry in Wilson’s discography, diverging from the more progressive rock-oriented albums that preceded it and embracing a more accessible, pop-inflected approach. The album received positive critical attention for its adventurous production and thoughtful lyrics, and it achieved notable chart success, reaching the Top 5 in several European countries, including Austria and the Netherlands. Its blend of personal introspection and social observation solidified its place as a significant release in Wilson’s catalog.
